newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates fall in week--FHLMC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates fall in week--FHLMC.

text.p: The average commitment rates on U.S. 30- and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages fell slightly in the week ending January 24 after rising for three consecutive weeks, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp said Thursday.
The 30-year interest rate inched down to an average 7.85 percent from 7.87 percent last week, while the 15-year fell to 7.35 percent from 7.38 percent.
Adjustable-rate mortgages were unchanged at 5.57 percent in the week.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.00 percent, the 15-year 6.50 percent and the ARM 5.37 percent.

Frank Nothaft, Freddie Mac deputy chief economist, said the modest 0.3 percent rise in the December Consumer Price Index "helped to quell fears of inflation, thus mortgage rates remained basically unchanged from the prior week."
"We envision the 30-year fixed rate staying stable over the next few weeks, in the affordable 7.5 percent to eight percent range," Nothaft added.

On Wednesday, the Commerce Department said U.S. December housing starts fell 12.2 percent to a 1.329 million unit annual rate. But it also said housing starts for all of 1996, at an annual rate of 1.474 million units, were the strongest level for any year since 1988.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.8 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.8 percent on the 15-year, up from 1.7 percent last week and 1.4 percent on the ARM, unchanged from last week.
